headline: Bitcoin climbs 2.3% back above 60,000 dollars after Friday's AI rout sank the Nasdaq 5.3%
subhead: The S&P 500 sits 11.6% below its 52-week high after Friday's 3.7% drop and Nvidia's 14.0% slide, while India's Nifty rose 1.1% to 25,800.6; US PCE inflation on 25 November leads a Thanksgiving-shortened week.

us.text: S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.4, now 11.6% below its 52-week high, and the Nasdaq 5.3% as Anthropic's second-day slide deepened the AI unwind.
Nvidia fell 14.0% to a 52-week low of 125.53, with Arm down 14.1%, Micron 13.9% and AMD 13.2% in a chip rout.
A holiday-shortened week turns on October PCE inflation, GDP and durable goods on 25 November, with markets closed for Thanksgiving on 26 November.

india.text: Nifty rose 1.1% to 25,800.6 and Sensex 1.1% to 83,919.7 on Friday as banks led; Bank Nifty gained 2.5% to a record 64,635.2.
FIIs net bought 10,308.4 crore rupees in cash on Friday while DIIs net sold 4,859.8 crore, per provisional data.
The rupee firmed past 93 per dollar on Friday for the first time since April; the feed shows USD/INR at 92.67, down 0.7%.

global.text: Nikkei 225 closed at 56,436.7 and the Kospi at 4,870.0 on Friday as the chip selloff spread; Hang Seng ended at 22,410.8.
Stoxx 600 fell 2.0% to 625.65 on Friday, capping its worst week since March as ASML and Infineon slumped.
Bitcoin rebounded from a two-year low of 55,130 dollars to about 60,134, up 2.3%, after 1.8 billion dollars of liquidations cleared forced selling.

weekly.narrative: An AI unwind dominated the week: Anthropic's record Nasdaq debut failed to steady sentiment, Nvidia fell 22.9 percent and the Nasdaq 10.0 percent, its worst week since March 2020, while the S&P 500 lost 8.6 percent and closed in correction. Near-certain bets on a December Fed hike pushed gold down 9.5 percent and silver 16.3 percent to 52-week lows, and bitcoin fell 7.9 percent toward its 2026 low. India stood apart as heavy foreign buying lifted the Nifty to a nine-month high of 25,800.6 and Bank Nifty to records, while Tokyo, Seoul and Frankfurt followed Wall Street lower. Next week is shortened by Thanksgiving and turns on US PCE inflation and GDP on 25 November, ahead of the Fed decision on 9 December.
